pr_title: fix(ivy): add attributes and classes to host elements based on selector
pr_body:
In View Engine, host element of dynamically created component received attributes and classes extracted from component's selector. For example, if component selector is `[attr] .class`, the `attr` attribute and `.class` class will be add to host element. This commit adds similar logic to Ivy, to make sure this behavior is aligned with View Engine.

This PR resolves #35445.

## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix


## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

review_comments:
There are three cases that I know of: 

1) User creates component dynamically with `ViewContainerRef.createComponent` or `ComponentFactory.create` (with no selector).  In this case, we will create the component, so we should be adding appropriate attrs / classes to the new element. (This is the case outlined in the Github issue)

2) App is bootstrapping. `ApplicationRef` will call `ComponentFactory.create` with the selector found in the component factory. Because there's a selector, we will locate the correct host element using the selector. In this case, we should not be adding attrs / classes (if we've located it based on the selector, it already has those attrs/classes, so it's wasted work).

3) User creates a component dynamically using `ComponentFactory.create` and passes in a selector. This selector will be used to locate the host element in which to bootstrap the component. In this case, I think we should also avoid adding attrs / classes. We should treat the passed selector as a replacement for the component's selector and ignore what is in the component selector. Otherwise, we could run into cases where the passed selector and the component def's selector don't match and there's no way to reconcile the two (e.g. if they both have tag selectors like 'my-comp').

In this PR, it looks like we would add the attrs / classes in all 3 cases. At the least, I think we should avoid adding attrs / classes in case 2 (bootstrap). I think it's most correct to also avoid adding attrs in case 3 as well, e.g.

```suggestion
      if (hostRNode && !rootSelectorOrNode) {
```

but it looks like a minor breaking change to VE. I'd argue that it's actually a bug fix because the behavior here doesn't make sense. 

What do you think of the 3 cases?

Thanks for review @kara!

Your proposal makes a lot of sense.

From `ComponentFactory.create` standpoint we should consider 2 cases:

- when **selector or host node is passed** into the function, which means that host node already exists on a page and we just "insert" our component into it. Since that node was already created (inside or outside of the framework), I think we should not "touch" it and just perform component bootstrap.

- when **selector or host node is not passed** into the function - we create a host node ourselves and in this case it makes sense to add attributes and classes based on selector.

The main motivation for the current implementation was to match VE behavior as closely as possible, but I agree that having different logic based on selector presence makes more sense.

I would also argue for only adding attrs for the case (1) [as outlined by Kara](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34481#discussion_r379682699).

I think that there reasoning of "we don't touch a host node if we don't create it" is very reasonable.
@pkozlowski-opensource You mean only add attrs in case 1? Case 2 is the bootstrap case.
@kara sorry, this is what I've meant... My brain is half half-asleep today. Edited my comment...

@kara and @pkozlowski-opensource thanks for reviewing this PR. I've applied the necessary changes to avoid adding attrs/classes in case selector is provided. Could you please take another look when you get a chance? Thank you.
